evidence.title: Replace the accumulate loop in TagNormaliser with array functions
evidence.why: The loop does a linear `in_array` scan per tag. The one-expression form keeps the `list<string>` return type without a temp or `@var`. `array_unique` compares as strings, which matches the strict check for string input, and the explicit callback keeps the tag '0' (a bare `array_filter` would drop it). The existing test with '0', '00', '1e3' and '1000' still passes.
evidence.suggested: return array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map(trim(...), $tags), fn (string $tag): bool => $tag !== '')));

evidence.title: Remove unused ProductCodes, AllowedHosts and the unregistered TrimStrings
evidence.why: Nothing calls `ProductCodes` or `AllowedHosts`; only their tests do. `TrimStrings` is never registered, and its `$except` repeats the framework class's own defaults (read in vendor), so removing it changes nothing. Confirm with the team that no pending feature needs the two helpers before deleting. Both helpers are also near-duplicates of `TagNormaliser`. The suite goes from 11 to 9 tests at this step.

evidence.title: Use #[Fillable] without accepted and add casts on Offer and Order
evidence.why: `User` already uses the Laravel 13 attributes, while `Offer` and `Order` use the property, so the codebase has two styles. `accepted` is a state the API should not set, yet it is mass-assignable, and neither model casts its numeric or boolean columns. Factories bypass fillable, so the tests are unaffected.

evidence.title: Aggregate revenue per country in SQL instead of loading every order
evidence.why: The report hydrates every order into memory to add up one column, so memory and time grow with the table. The database can return one row per country; the `(int)` map keeps the declared `array<string, int>` because some drivers return SUM as a string. The existing test and an added empty-table test pass, and PHPStan level 8 stays clean.
evidence.suggested:
return Order::query()
            ->selectRaw('country, sum(total_cents) as total')
            ->groupBy('country')
            ->orderBy('country')
            ->pluck('total', 'country')
            ->map(fn (mixed $total): int => (int) $total)
            ->all();
